li.label: copied the old writing
li.description: Three days in the hill, copying the vault walls by lamplight. Every line is on paper now, and my hand still won't straighten.

li.label: the sleeper stayed
li.description: The sleeper from the hill is staying with us. Every day there's a new question about a war that ended before I was born.

li.label: a debt repaid
li.description: The stranger we hid that night came back with a clean name and paid us more than was owed. I'd stopped expecting to see that face again.

li.label: gave up an innocent
li.description: We told the riders which way the stranger ran, and the stranger had done nothing wrong. I'd give a lot to take that answer back.

li.label: a wedding at our place
li.description: The couple from the feuding families were married here, with both heads of house sharing the feast. I danced until my feet hurt.

li.label: the talks failed
li.description: I tried to make peace between those two families, and it ended in blood. I keep going over what I should have said.

li.label: the preacher's sermon
li.description: I went to hear the preacher on the road. I don't know if I believe a word of it, but I slept well afterward.

li.label: won the argument
li.description: I took on the preacher with a crowd watching, and it was the preacher who ran out of answers first.

li.label: lost the argument
li.description: The preacher had an answer ready for everything I said, with the whole yard listening. I've thought of three good replies since.

li.label: kept from following
li.description: I was ready to walk the road with the preacher. The preacher's gone on without me, and my bag is still packed under the bed.

li.label: arguments at supper
li.description: Every supper turns into an argument about the preacher's words. I just want to eat.

li.label: talked it out
li.description: The quarrel over the preacher's words has run its course. Both sides ate together at supper and passed each other the bread.

li.label: the rescue came back
li.description: The rescue we outfitted dug through the rockfall and brought the living out of that ruin. I keep picturing them stepping out into the daylight.

li.label: pilgrims at our shrine
li.description: Pilgrims knelt in a ring around the sculpture we put up and prayed there, a long way from home. One of them laid a hand on it before they left.
